description: Trusted SAS code: how a .sas file becomes measures, how a call's arguments become the SAS that precedes the measure's code, and how a SAS log is read for failure. A measure block is a comment opening with `/**` at the start of a line and closing at the first `*/`, holding an `@measure` tag. Inside it, each line loses its leading whitespace and one leading `*`, and is then trimmed. Prose before the first tag is split into paragraphs at blank lines, each paragraph's lines joined by a single space: the first is the title, the rest the description. A tag's text runs on over following lines (joined by a space) until a blank line or the next tag. Tags: `@measure [name]` (the name defaults to the file stem), `@param name|[name]|[name=default] [`type`] text` (brackets mark an optional argument; the type code span is one of `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum[a, b]`, or any of those followed by `[]` for an array, and defaults to string; array arguments take no default), `@return text`, `@output LIBREF.TABLE|TABLE|none` (default WORK.RESULT; a bare table is in WORK; `none` returns the listing), and repeatable `@provenance url`. The description the model reads is the title, the description, and `Returns: ` plus the return text, joined by blank lines. A measure's code runs from its block's `*/` to the next measure block or the end of the file; text before the first measure block is shared preamble, prepended to every measure's code with a blank line between. Code is trimmed of leading and trailing blank lines, and CRLF is read as LF. Errors are pinned as slugs, because the wording belongs to each language.

cases.name: a minimal measure takes its name from the file stem
cases.text:
/**
 * Number of students
 *
 * @measure
 * @output none
 */
proc sql; select count(*) from sashelp.class; quit;

expected.name: class_count
expected.title: Number of students
expected.code: proc sql; select count(*) from sashelp.class; quit;

cases.name: typed, optional, and defaulted arguments
cases.text:
/** Regional revenue
 *
 * Revenue summed over a region's orders,
 * net of returns.
 *
 * @measure region_revenue
 * @param region `enum[EMEA, AMER]` The sales region.
 * @param [year=2025] `integer` Fiscal year.
 * @param [cap] `number` Upper bound
 *   on order value.
 * @param [net=true] `boolean` Net of returns.
 * @param [label=All orders] Report label.
 * @return One row with the total.
 * @output WORK.REVENUE
 * @provenance https://example.com/revenue.sas
 */
proc sql;
  create table work.revenue as select sum(amount) as total from sales where region = "&region";
quit;

expected.name: region_revenue
expected.title: Regional revenue
expected.description:
Regional revenue

Revenue summed over a region's orders, net of returns.

Returns: One row with the total.

schema.description: A parsed SAS measure renders through the same measure_schema_text as any other, so a .sas file and an equivalent R or Python measure read identically to the model.

cases.name: a SAS measure's schema block
cases.text:
/** Regional revenue
 * @measure
 * @param region `enum[EMEA, AMER]` The sales region.
 * @param [year=2025] `integer` Fiscal year.
 * @param [products] `string[]` Product codes.
 * @return One row.
 */
run;
cases.expected:
### revenue
Regional revenue

Returns: One row.

arguments:
  - region (one of {EMEA, AMER}, required) The sales region.
  - year (integer, optional) Fiscal year.
  - products (array of {string}, optional) Product codes.

prelude.description: The SAS submitted ahead of a measure's code for one call. `values` holds every declared argument after defaults are applied; null is an optional argument left unset. Every declared argument is assigned on every call, so a value from an earlier call in the same SAS session cannot leak into this one. Values are assigned with CALL SYMPUTX from single-quoted literals (quotes doubled), so nothing in a value is resolved as a macro at assignment: strings and enums are the value itself, integers are decimal, numbers are printf %.15g, booleans are 1 or 0, null is empty, and an array is its elements as SAS literals separated by a space (strings single-quoted, ready for `in (&name)`). A measure with an output table first deletes it, so a stale table from an earlier call cannot be returned.

log_errors.description: A SAS run fails when its log has a line starting `ERROR` followed by an optional message number and a colon. Those lines, trimmed of trailing whitespace, are what a failure reports. A warning, or ERROR in the middle of a line, is not a failure.

cases.name: a clean log
cases.log:
NOTE: The data set WORK.RESULT has 19 observations.
WARNING: Apparent symbolic reference X not resolved.

cases.name: errors with and without a message number

ERROR 180-322: Statement is not valid or it is used out of proper order.  
NOTE: PROC SQL set option NOEXEC.
ERROR: File WORK.NOPE.DATA does not exist.
expected: ERROR 180-322: Statement is not valid or it is used out of proper order.
ERROR: File WORK.NOPE.DATA does not exist.
